From ea75a342aed5ed72c87f38fbe0df2f5df7eae374 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: James Clark <james.clark@arm.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Jan 2022 11:30:47 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] coresight: Fix TRCCONFIGR.QE sysfs interface

It's impossible to program a valid value for TRCCONFIGR.QE
when TRCIDR0.QSUPP==0b10. In that case the following is true:

  Q element support is implemented, and only supports Q elements without
  instruction counts. TRCCONFIGR.QE can only take the values 0b00 or 0b11.

Currently the low bit of QSUPP is checked to see if the low bit of QE can
be written to, but as you can see when QSUPP==0b10 the low bit is cleared
making it impossible to ever write the only valid value of 0b11 to QE.
0b10 would be written instead, which is a reserved QE value even for all
values of QSUPP.

The fix is to allow writing the low bit of QE for any non zero value of
QSUPP.

This change also ensures that the low bit is always set, even when the
user attempts to only set the high bit.

Signed-off-by: James Clark <james.clark@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Mike Leach <mike.leach@linaro.org>
Fixes: d8c66962084f ("coresight-etm4x: Controls pertaining to the reset, mode, pe and events")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220120113047.2839622-2-james.clark@arm.com
Signed-off-by: Mathieu Poirier <mathieu.poirier@linaro.org>
Signed-off-by: Suzuki K Poulose <suzuki.poulose@arm.com>

diff --git a/drivers/hwtracing/coresight/coresight-etm4x-sysfs.c b/drivers/hwtracing/coresight/coresight-etm4x-sysfs.c
index a0640fa5c55b..57e94424a8d6 100644
--- a/drivers/hwtracing/coresight/coresight-etm4x-sysfs.c
+++ b/drivers/hwtracing/coresight/coresight-etm4x-sysfs.c
@@ -367,8 +367,12 @@ static ssize_t mode_store(struct device *dev,
 	mode = ETM_MODE_QELEM(config->mode);
 	/* start by clearing QE bits */
 	config->cfg &= ~(BIT(13) | BIT(14));
-	/* if supported, Q elements with instruction counts are enabled */
-	if ((mode & BIT(0)) && (drvdata->q_support & BIT(0)))
+	/*
+	 * if supported, Q elements with instruction counts are enabled.
+	 * Always set the low bit for any requested mode. Valid combos are
+	 * 0b00, 0b01 and 0b11.
+	 */
+	if (mode && drvdata->q_support)
 		config->cfg |= BIT(13);
 	/*
 	 * if supported, Q elements with and without instruction
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `coresight-etm4x-sysfs.c`**
   - The code block that checks if Q elements with instruction counts are enabled has been modified.
   - The condition now checks if `mode` is non-zero and if `drvdata->q_support` is true, allowing the low bit of `QE` to be set for any non-zero value of `QSUPP`.
   - The comment has been updated to clarify that valid combinations for `QE` are `0b00`, `0b01`, and `0b11`, ensuring that the low bit is always set when a mode is requested.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `coresight-etm4x-sysfs.c` directly addresses the bug related to the `TRCCONFIGR.QE` sysfs interface by ensuring that the low bit of `QE` can be written correctly when `QSUPP` is non-zero. This change prevents the writing of reserved values and aligns the behavior of the code with the hardware specifications, thus fixing the underlying issue described in the patch.

This leads to the inability to write the valid value `0b11` to `QE`, resulting in a reserved value being written instead. The second statement clears the QE bits, and the third statement attempts to set the low bit of `QE` based on the incorrect condition, which fails when `QSUPP` is `0b10`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (mode && drvdata->q_support)
```
```c
config->cfg |= BIT(13);
```
Reason:
The first statement allows the low bit of `QE` to be set for any non-zero value of `QSUPP`, ensuring that valid combinations (0b00, 0b01, and 0b11) can be written to `QE`. The second statement sets the low bit of `QE` correctly, thus fixing the issue of writing a reserved value when `QSUPP` is `0b10`.
